"""Build Draft v1 of the Performance Technology Best Practices guide and its forms.

Outputs (deliverables/):
    SSI_BestPractices_GUIDE_DRAFTv1_ER_<DATE>.docx + .pdf         the guide
    SSI_BestPractices_APPX_<X>_<name>_ER_<DATE>.docx + .pdf      forms A-E

Guide content lives here; form content lives in scripts/forms.py.
    python scripts/build_guide.py
"""
import sys
from pathlib import Path

HERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
DEV = HERE.parent
sys.path.insert(0, str(DEV / "Baylor_Doc_Style"))
sys.path.insert(0, str(DEV / "Tech_Inventory_Analysis" / "scripts"))
sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent))
from baylor_docstyle import BaylorDoc  # noqa: E402
from doc_platform import word_pdf      # noqa: E402
from forms import FORMS, ACCESS_HEAD, ACCESS_MATRIX  # noqa: E402

DATE = "2026-10-07"
NAME = f"SSI_BestPractices_GUIDE_DRAFTv2_ER_{DATE}"


def guide():
    d = BaylorDoc("Performance Technology Best Practices",
                  deck="How Baylor Athletics chooses, uses and protects performance "
                       "technology and the athlete data it produces. Baylor's written plan "
                       "under the NCAA SSI recommendations.",
                  status="Draft v2 for discussion")
    d.meta([
        ["Status", "**Draft v2** for discussion. Items marked [Pending …] wait on the named review."],
        ["Date", "October 7, 2026"],
        ["For", "Kenny Boyd"],
        ["Source", "NCAA SSI Performance Technologies Recommendations (March 2026); "
                   "SSI webinar of September 9, 2026; Applied Performance practice and records"],
        ["Prepared by", "Applied Performance, Baylor Athletics"],
        ["Owner", "Applied Performance (Data Steward). Approved by Kenny Boyd. [Pending Kenny: approval.]"],
        ["Companions", "Appendices A to E (separate forms); SSI crosswalk; "
                       "Software and Technology Management Framework"],
    ])
    d.callout("Statement of practice",
              "This guide is the standard operating procedure of Baylor Athletics for choosing "
              "and using performance technology and handling the athlete data it produces. It "
              "applies to every unit that collects athlete performance or physiologic data, and "
              "to the vendors that hold that data. It describes the expected way of working. "
              "Where a unit or project departs from it, the reason is noted at the next "
              "Technology Review (Section 1.1) so the guide can improve; a departure is not "
              "penalised. Athletic Medicine holds authority over physiologic data and over "
              "medical and return-to-play decisions (Section 1.4). Applied Performance keeps the "
              "guide current and leads its annual review (Section 7). "
              "**Approved:** Kenny Boyd ________________  **Date:** __________ "
              "[Pending Kenny: approval and scope.]")
    d.callout("How to read this draft",
              "Sections 0 to 7 are the guide. The forms it refers to (A to E) are separate "
              "documents. Where a position needs a decision from you, General Counsel (OGC), "
              "ITS, Procurement or Athletic Medicine, the draft takes a position and marks it, "
              "for example **[Pending OGC]**, so review can happen without stopping the work. "
              "Positions marked [Pending Kenny] are Applied Performance's recommendation. "
              "References such as SSI Rec 3.2 point to the NCAA recommendation each part meets.")

    # 0 -------------------------------------------------------------------
    d.section("0.  Purpose and scope", numbered=False)
    d.para("In March 2026 the NCAA Sport Science Institute (SSI) published Performance "
           "Technologies Recommendations: Responsible Use in Collegiate Athletics. It asks "
           "every school to keep a written plan covering how technology is chosen, how athlete "
           "data is managed, how people are educated, and how the plan improves. This guide is "
           "that plan for Baylor Athletics: a best-practices guide with procedures and forms "
           "that, taken as a whole, is the department's standard operating procedure (see the "
           "statement above). It sits beside the Software and Technology "
           "Management Framework (August 2026 draft): the framework, once adopted, runs the request and "
           "review process, and this guide supplies the parts the framework lists as "
           "\"planned for Version 1\". [Pending Kenny: this guide as the framework's Version 1; "
           "framework adopted.] The framework is still a draft. At "
           "its August 13 review ITS preferred that its content feed the existing ITS request "
           "process rather than run beside it; this guide works either way.")
    d.subhead("Definitions")
    d.table(["Term", "Meaning in this guide"], [
        ["Performance technology", "Any device or tool that collects biometric or performance data: wearables, sensors, force plates, cameras and video, surveys, software and mobile apps (SSI definition)."],
        ["Performance data", "Training and competition output: distance, speed, load, jump height, force, video and tactics."],
        ["Physiologic data", "Data about the body's state: heart rate and HRV, sleep, body composition, wellness scores, injury and rehabilitation measures. Handled as health data."],
        ["Cognitive data", "Results of cognitive or perceptual testing, such as S2 Cognition."],
        ["Notice", "Telling athletes what is collected in team settings, why, and who sees it."],
        ["Consent", "An athlete's written yes, freely given and revocable, before data is collected."],
        ["Data Steward", "The person who keeps this guide running day to day (Section 1.2)."],
        ["Custodian", "The named person responsible for one platform's data and accounts (Section 6)."],
    ], widths=[1.6, 5.1])
    d.subhead("Who it applies to")
    d.para("Every Baylor Athletics staff member, coach, analyst, intern and contractor who "
           "selects, runs, reads or shares performance technology data; every student-athlete "
           "whose data is collected; and every vendor that holds that data. Where a Baylor "
           "University policy already governs a type of data (FERPA records, protected health "
           "information, information security), that policy still governs.")
    d.subhead("Principles")
    d.bullets([
        "**Start from the question.** We buy and collect to answer a question someone will act on, not because a peer school has the product.",
        "**Data guided, not data driven.** Technology is one tool. It informs the judgment of coaches and clinicians; it does not replace it.",
        "**Collect only what we use.** If no one acts on a measure, we stop collecting it.",
        "**Athletic Medicine decides return to play.** No performance number overrides that authority.",
        "**Athletes know, and athletes choose.** Athletes are told what is collected in team settings, and say yes or no to the rest.",
    ])

    # 1 -------------------------------------------------------------------
    d.section("1.  Governance", numbered=False)
    d.subhead("1.1  Technology Review (SSI Rec 1.1, 4.3, 5.1)")
    d.para("Performance technology is a standing item at an existing departmental staff "
           "meeting, the **Technology Review**, rather than a new committee. When technology "
           "is on the agenda the people below take part, so decisions are made by a "
           "multidisciplinary group as SSI asks, and a student-athlete representative from "
           "SAAC is invited. Level 3 requests (Section 2) are decided at the Technology Review "
           "with Athletic Medicine taking part, and recorded on Appendix E before the Business "
           "Office and ITS reviews. Level 2 requests are decided by the Data Steward and the "
           "Director of Athletic Performance and reported at the next Technology Review. The "
           "Technology Review also runs the annual review (Section 7) and agrees changes to "
           "this guide and its forms. [Pending Kenny: which existing meeting.]")
    d.table(["Who takes part", "Why"], [
        ["Student-athlete (SAAC representative), invited when technology is on the agenda", "SSI names student-athletes first (Rec 1.1)"],
        ["Athletic Medicine: head athletic trainer or designee", "Physiologic data and return-to-play authority"],
        ["Athletic Performance: director or senior coach", "Runs most wearables and testing"],
        ["Applied Performance: director (Data Steward)", "Reporting, technology inventory, this guide"],
        ["Coaches: a sport representative", "End users of the data"],
        ["Administration: sport administrator or Business Office", "Budget and contract authority"],
        ["Consulted as needed: OGC, ITS, Risk Management, Compliance, Procurement", "Legal, security, risk and contract review (SSI Rec 3)"],
    ], widths=[3.9, 2.8])
    d.subhead("1.2  Data Steward")
    d.para("The Director of Applied Performance acts as Data Steward. The Steward keeps the "
           "technology inventory current, keeps the consent register, answers athlete and "
           "staff data questions, logs every outside data release, and runs the offboarding "
           "checklist with supervisors. A named backup Steward (the Director of Athletic "
           "Performance or designee) can run the register, the inventory and Appendix C. "
           "The Steward facilitates; each platform's custodian "
           "stays responsible for that platform (Section 6).")
    d.subhead("1.3  Review and version control")
    d.para("The Technology Review reviews this guide every spring using Appendix D, and again "
           "whenever the NCAA, the Big 12 or Baylor policy changes. Each version carries a "
           "number, date and revision log, and the master copy lives in a Baylor Athletics "
           "shared location, not a personal drive.")
    d.subhead("1.4  Medical authority (SSI Rec 3.3)")
    d.para("Baylor's primary athletics healthcare providers, the team physicians and athletic "
           "trainers of Athletic Medicine, hold unchallengeable, autonomous authority over "
           "medical management and return-to-play decisions (SSI Rec 3.3), consistent with the NCAA Independent "
           "Medical Care guidance. Performance data can inform those decisions; it cannot make "
           "or overturn them. A report that supports return to play uses thresholds set by "
           "Athletic Medicine, the athletic trainer records each phase change and the "
           "clearance, and the report itself makes no clearance "
           "decision. Coaches and administrators may not override a medical decision on the "
           "strength of technology data.")

    # 2 -------------------------------------------------------------------
    d.section("2.  Technology adoption", numbered=False)
    d.subhead("2.1  The process (SSI Rec 4, 4.3)")
    d.para("Once the framework is adopted, every new technology, trial, free tool or "
           "sponsor-supplied product goes through it: a Technology Idea Form and internal "
           "ATH Form; the Business Office as first control point; ITS as second; a "
           "documented decision; then implementation and a usage review at six months or "
           "season end. Until then, requests follow the existing ITS request process and "
           "the levels below apply to them. This guide does not repeat "
           "that process. It adds the question, the review levels below, and the forms.")
    d.table(["Review level (framework §6)", "Triggered by", "Added by this guide"], [
        ["Level 1 Standard", "No athlete data; one unit; low or one-time cost", "Appendix E Part 1 and gates only"],
        ["Level 2 Enhanced", "Performance data kept on Baylor systems; several teams; or recurring cost", "Full Appendix E; Data Steward and Director of Athletic Performance decide (Section 1.1)"],
        ["Level 3 Comprehensive", "Physiologic, health or cognitive data; data leaving Baylor; or athlete data a vendor hosts or processes", "Full Appendix E; Technology Review decision; Athletic Medicine sign-off; Appendix B before signature; consent check (Section 3)"],
    ], widths=[1.7, 2.5, 2.5])
    d.note("A requester who is unsure whether a product touches health data or sends data to "
           "a vendor answers \"yes\". This follows the Athletics routing sheet drafted after "
           "the August 13, 2026 review with ITS. It is the proposed working reading of the "
           "framework's level table; a Level 3 trigger wins over Level 2. "
           "[Pending ITS: confirm the routing sheet.]")
    d.subhead("2.2  Start from the question, and one scoring sheet (SSI Rec 4.1)")
    d.para("Appendix E opens with the question the technology will answer, who will act on "
           "it and how often. A request that cannot name a decision does not proceed. "
           "Appendix E is also the **single** scoring instrument. It merges the March 2026 "
           "evaluation checklist and the August 2026 Technology Evaluation Scorecard, which "
           "until now used different criteria: six pass-or-fail gates (fit to the question, compliance and "
           "privacy, ownership and exit, student-athlete impact, transparency, "
           "interoperability) and eight features rated Strong, Adequate or Weak, built on the "
           "Sports Tech Research Network quality framework.")
    d.subhead("2.3  Quality before commitment (SSI Rec 4.2)")
    d.bullets([
        "**Evidence.** Ask the vendor for independent, not vendor-funded, validation in an "
        "athletic population. Missing evidence is recorded as Weak, not assumed.",
        "**Black boxes.** Two devices can give different scores for the same session, and "
        "several published equations exist for some metrics. The vendor must explain how "
        "derived scores are calculated (an Appendix E gate).",
        "**Trial.** Where evidence is weak, run a 30 to 60 day trial with one team and a hard "
        "end date, then report to the Technology Review at 90 days.",
        "**Peer check.** Ask at least two comparable programs about their experience.",
        "**Consolidate first.** A request for a new product names anything we already own "
        "that does the same job, using the technology inventory.",
    ])

    # 3 -------------------------------------------------------------------
    d.section("3.  Athlete consent and education", numbered=False)
    d.subhead("3.1  Notice and consent (SSI Foundational: rights; Rec 2)")
    d.para("Some collection is part of being on a team and cannot be switched off for one "
           "athlete: video of practice, venue or team tracking during sessions, and testing "
           "that is part of the training program. For these, Baylor gives clear **notice**. "
           "Other collection needs the athlete's **consent** before it starts.")
    d.table(["Notice (told, not asked)", "Consent (asked; can say no)"], [
        ["Practice and competition video", "Wearables worn outside team sessions (heart rate, HRV, sleep)"],
        ["Team GPS or venue tracking in sessions (e.g. Catapult, Kinexon)", "Body composition (DEXA or similar)"],
        ["Force plate and jump testing in the training program", "Cognitive testing (e.g. S2)"],
        ["Wellness check-ins used by Athletic Medicine; vendor norm pooling Baylor has agreed to in writing", "Research use; release beyond Baylor's contracted vendors"],
    ], widths=[3.35, 3.35])
    d.para("Saying no has no effect on scholarship, playing time or place on the team, and "
           "consent can be withdrawn in writing at any time. [Pending OGC: which items sit "
           "under notice and which under consent, and whether team GPS and testing need "
           "consent under Texas law.]")
    d.subhead("3.2  The consent form and when it is signed")
    d.bullets([
        "Appendix A is signed by every student-athlete at the start of each academic year, "
        "and again when a new technology is introduced in their sport.",
        "Each sport attaches the list of technologies it uses, kept by its Athletic "
        "Performance coach and checked against the technology inventory.",
        "Athletes under 18 also need a parent or guardian signature.",
        "The form is reviewed by OGC before first use. [Pending OGC: final wording.]",
    ])
    d.subhead("3.3  Vendor norm-building")
    d.para("Many vendors pool de-identified customer data to build norms. Under Appendix B "
           "(row 6) a vendor may pool Baylor data only where Baylor has agreed in writing, "
           "and Appendix A tells athletes which vendors have that agreement. Where a "
           "vendor can leave out individual athletes, Appendix A gives them that choice. "
           "[Pending vendors: which can exclude individual athletes.] "
           "On small rosters de-identification is weak, since a staff member can often "
           "tell which athlete is which, so pooling is treated as a release of athlete "
           "data.")
    d.subhead("3.4  Where consent records live")
    d.para("Signed forms are kept with the athlete's Athletic Medicine record, and the Data "
           "Steward keeps a register of who has consented to what, so staff can check before "
           "collecting. [Pending Athletic Medicine: system of record, for example the "
           "department athlete management system.]")
    d.subhead("3.5  Education (SSI Rec 2, 2.1 to 2.3)")
    d.para("Education is what makes consent informed, so it sits in this section. Applied "
           "Performance builds the materials and delivers them to each group at least once a "
           "year (SSI Rec 2.1), tailored to what that group needs (Rec 2.2).")
    d.table(["Audience", "Format", "When"], [
        ["All staff using or seeing the data", "Short session or recorded module", "Each year, before fall camp"],
        ["Student-athletes", "Team briefing and a one-page handout with Appendix A", "When consent is signed, and when a new technology is introduced"],
        ["Coaches", "Briefing on what they can and cannot see", "Each year"],
        ["New staff, interns, contractors", "Recorded module", "Within 30 days of start"],
    ], widths=[2.2, 2.4, 2.1])
    d.para("Every session covers SSI's four topics, at the depth each audience needs: "
           "(1) limitations and possible harms, including fixation on numbers, leaderboards "
           "and body-image concerns; (2) privacy and security; (3) athlete rights, including "
           "consent and how to raise a concern; (4) this guide and its forms. Coaches also "
           "learn what they can and cannot see, and that medical decisions are not theirs; "
           "Athletic Performance and Applied Performance staff cover data quality and when to "
           "escalate to Athletic Medicine. Materials live in a Baylor Athletics shared "
           "location and are updated at the annual review. Attendance is recorded and "
           "reported in the annual review.")

    # 4 -------------------------------------------------------------------
    d.section("4.  Data management", numbered=False)
    d.subhead("4.1  Ownership and rights (SSI Rec 3, 3.2)")
    d.para("**Draft position:** ownership follows the type of data. Each athlete owns their "
           "physiologic data, and Baylor holds and uses it on their behalf under this guide "
           "and Appendix A. Baylor owns performance data, and each athlete has the right to "
           "see and receive a copy of their own. Against any vendor, the data belongs to "
           "Baylor and its athletes, never to the vendor (Appendix B). This matches the "
           "framework. If OGC prefers Baylor ownership of all data, the athlete's access "
           "rights stay as written. [Pending Kenny/OGC: ownership position.] Either way, physiologic "
           "data is treated as health information and may be protected under HIPAA, FERPA or "
           "Texas law, while performance data such as a sprint time is usually not. "
           "International athletes, and vendors that store data outside the United States, may "
           "also bring other countries' law into play (SSI: rights and protections). "
           "[Pending OGC: classification under HIPAA, FERPA, Texas and applicable international law.]")
    d.subhead("4.2  Storage: what we hold and where")
    d.table(["Data class", "Examples", "Where it is kept"], [
        ["Performance", "GPS and venue tracking, force plates, video", "Vendor platform under contract; Baylor-controlled storage for reports and analysis"],
        ["Performance used in return to play", "Force plate or jump testing in a return-to-play plan", "As physiologic data, below"],
        ["Physiologic / medical", "Heart rate and HRV, sleep, body composition, injury and rehabilitation records", "Athletic Medicine systems, or Baylor storage restricted to Athletic Medicine and named staff; only aggregate figures leave them"],
        ["Cognitive", "Cognitive or perceptual testing", "Vendor platform; restricted Baylor storage for analysis"],
    ], widths=[1.6, 2.4, 2.7])
    d.bullets([
        "Identifiable athlete data lives only on vendor platforms under contract and on "
        "Baylor-controlled storage. It must not go into code repositories, personal cloud "
        "accounts, email attachments to outside addresses, or chat and AI tools that are "
        "not approved by ITS.",
        "Reports and analysis that leave Applied Performance use the least identifiable form "
        "that does the job: team or position summaries where they will do.",
        "Every storage location is listed in the technology inventory with its custodian. "
        "[Pending ITS: approved storage tiers for health data.]",
    ])
    d.subhead("4.3  Access (SSI Rec 3)")
    d.table(ACCESS_HEAD, ACCESS_MATRIX, widths=[1.6, 1.0, 1.3, 1.0, 0.9, 0.9])
    d.subhead("4.4  Who interprets and communicates (SSI Rec 3.1)")
    d.para("Health and physiologic data are interpreted and communicated by appropriately "
           "licensed Athletic Medicine staff (physicians, athletic trainers). Applied "
           "Performance may prepare reports under their oversight but does not make "
           "clinical interpretations. Athletic Performance and Applied Performance staff "
           "interpret training-load and performance data after the annual session and the "
           "vendor's operator training where one exists. The Data Steward keeps the "
           "competency record. The Head Athletic Trainer oversees health-data "
           "interpretation and the Director of Athletic Performance oversees "
           "performance-data interpretation. Coaches receive a \"summary with context\": a "
           "report built by Athletic or Applied Performance that may name athletes and "
           "carries the interpreter's reading, never a raw vendor dashboard. Wellness "
           "flags are the one exception to coaches seeing no medical data. Individual data "
           "is never posted publicly, ranked on public leaderboards, or used in broadcasts "
           "or media without the athlete's written consent.")
    d.subhead("4.5  Permitted and prohibited uses (SSI Rec 3.3)")
    d.table(["Permitted", "Prohibited"], [
        ["Managing training load and recovery", "Punishing or publicly shaming an athlete with data"],
        ["Supporting injury prevention and return to play (Athletic Medicine decides)", "Overriding a medical decision with performance data"],
        ["Evaluating training programs", "Scholarship or roster decisions on technology data alone"],
        ["Giving athletes their own data", "Sharing individual data with media, agents, pro teams or NIL partners without written consent"],
        ["Research, with IRB approval and separate consent", "Selling data or trading it for a price discount"],
        ["Recruiting evaluation using data the athlete has released", "Keeping data past the retention period without a legal reason"],
    ], widths=[3.35, 3.35])
    d.para("**Collect only what we use.** Each measure we collect is tied to a decision in the "
           "intake form. If the annual review finds no one acting on it, collection stops.")
    d.subhead("4.6  Transfer athletes (SSI Rec 3.2)")
    d.para("A transfer athlete's data moves between schools only with a release signed by "
           "both institutions and the athlete's written authorization, and only after the "
           "sport's staff confirm. The vendor moves the data; staff do not export and "
           "re-upload it.")
    d.bullets([
        "**Outgoing.** No Baylor data goes to another school, a pro team or an agent without "
        "the athlete's written request. The athlete can always have a copy of their own data.",
        "**Incoming.** Baylor requests data from a previous school only with the athlete's "
        "signed authorization, plus the two-school release. Athletic Medicine reviews "
        "incoming health data before it enters Baylor systems.",
        "**Logging.** The Data Steward logs every release in or out: what, to whom, on whose "
        "authority.",
        "**Deletion and retention.** Departing athletes may ask for deletion, subject to "
        "legal retention. [Pending OGC: retention period.]",
    ])

    # 5 -------------------------------------------------------------------
    d.section("5.  Vendor data contracts", numbered=False)
    d.para("SSI does not cover contracts, but the September 9 SSI webinar made the risk "
           "plain: vendors offer discounts in exchange for data, pool customer data into "
           "norms, and the staff using the product, including Athletic Medicine, may not "
           "know the contract says so. The August framework draft asks Procurement to "
           "address ownership, permitted use, storage, access, sharing, AI training, "
           "retention, deletion, portability and breach notice in contracts for products "
           "holding athlete data. This section turns that proposal into a checklist.")
    d.subhead("5.1  The standard addendum")
    d.para("Appendix B lists 14 terms. Six must be met before Baylor signs or renews a contract "
           "for a product that holds athlete data: Baylor ownership, permitted use only, "
           "**return and deletion at exit**, breach notification, no AI training on Baylor "
           "data without opt-in, and no data-for-discount or undisclosed norm pooling. "
           "[Pending OGC/Procurement: approved addendum wording.]")
    d.subhead("5.2  The exit clause")
    d.para("Nothing in Baylor's current process requires a vendor to return or delete data when "
           "a product is dropped. Under this guide, "
           "every discontinuation decision (framework Phase 3) triggers a written request for "
           "export and certified deletion, filed by the custodian.")
    d.subhead("5.3  Auditing existing contracts")
    d.para("The 2026 technology inventory found 188 products across all 32 units, 75 of them "
           "likely handling athlete data, and earlier legal "
           "discussions put active vendor relationships above 50. Auditing all of them by "
           "December is not realistic, so the audit runs by priority, using the inventory's "
           "contract columns (term end, auto-renew, notice days) to time each review before "
           "renewal:")
    d.numbered([
        "Wearables and tracking holding physiologic data (heart rate, HRV, sleep).",
        "Force plates and testing platforms.",
        "GPS and venue tracking (Catapult, Kinexon).",
        "Cognitive, body composition and athlete management systems.",
        "Everything else that touches athlete data, at its next renewal.",
    ])
    d.note("[Pending Procurement: who runs the audit, and whether the May 2026 outside-counsel "
           "proposal on vendor risk is still live.]")

    # 6 -------------------------------------------------------------------
    d.section("6.  Staff-transition continuity", numbered=False)
    d.para("Neither SSI nor the framework says what happens when the person who runs a system "
           "leaves. Data pipelines, databases, scheduled jobs and reports are often built and "
           "run by one or two people, sometimes on one machine or under individual accounts. "
           "A departure mid-season can stop them when they are most needed. The rules below "
           "make every system survive the departure of the "
           "person who knows it best.")
    d.subhead("6.1  Institutional accounts")
    d.para("Every vendor platform's admin account belongs to a Baylor institutional address or "
           "a shared departmental mailbox, never to an individual's personal or Baylor email. "
           "Code, scripts, report templates and scheduled jobs live in Baylor-owned locations "
           "and run under service accounts where ITS allows. Existing platforms are moved over "
           "during the contract audit (Section 5.3). [Pending ITS: shared mailbox and "
           "service-account options.]")
    d.subhead("6.2  A custodian and a backup for every platform")
    d.para("Each platform in the inventory has a named custodian and a named backup. The backup "
           "can log in, run a normal report end to end, and knows where credentials are held. "
           "The custodian also keeps the vendor contact, renewal date and licence count "
           "current in the inventory.")
    d.subhead("6.3  Handover notes")
    d.para("For each system a person runs, they keep a one-page note: what it does, how data "
           "gets in, how reports are built and sent and to whom, where credentials are, and "
           "known problems. It is updated when the system changes, not written in the last week.")
    d.subhead("6.4  Departure")
    d.para("When a staff member who uses or runs performance technology gives notice, the "
           "supervisor and Data Steward start Appendix C. Access is removed on every platform "
           "on the last working day, shared credentials and API keys are rotated, local copies "
           "of athlete data are returned or deleted with written confirmation, and the backup "
           "proves they can run each system before sign-off. The same checklist applies to "
           "interns and contractors. [Pending ITS: access-removal timeline.]")

    # 7 -------------------------------------------------------------------
    d.section("7.  Continuous improvement", numbered=False)
    d.subhead("7.1  The annual cycle (SSI Rec 5, 5.1)")
    d.para("Each spring the Technology Review, led by Applied Performance, which wrote this guide, "
           "gathers the year's feedback and reviews every technology, the education program "
           "and the guide itself with Appendix D. It ends with a decision for each "
           "technology (continue, modify or stop), a revised guide, and a one-page report to "
           "the document owner. The technology reviews line up with the framework's Phase 3 "
           "usage review, so a product is not judged twice.")
    d.subhead("7.2  Student-athlete feedback (SSI Rec 5.2)")
    d.bullets([
        "A short annual survey (about 13 questions) at the end of the spring semester: whether "
        "athletes understand what is collected and who sees it, whether they feel free to say "
        "no, whether the technology helped, and how often data caused them stress or anxiety.",
        "One SAAC focus group each year, across sports.",
        "A confidential channel for concerns at any time, through the Data Steward or a SAAC "
        "representative, open from spring 2027.",
        "Results and the changes made are reported back to athletes through SAAC.",
    ])
    d.subhead("7.3  Staff and effectiveness feedback (SSI Rec 5.3)")
    d.para("A short staff survey covers reliability, training and usefulness. Each technology is "
           "checked against the question it was bought to answer, using utilization data from "
           "the framework's Phase 3 review: if we are not acting on the data, we stop "
           "collecting it or stop paying for it. Education is judged on attendance and on "
           "what the surveys show people still do not know.")
    d.subhead("Timeline to in use")
    d.table(["By", "Step"], [
        ["Oct 14, 2026", "Plan agreed with Kenny; three decisions settled"],
        ["Oct 24, 2026", "Input from OGC, Procurement, ITS, Athletic Medicine"],
        ["Nov 6, 2026", "First draft to Kenny, revised from the October 4 working draft after OGC, Procurement, ITS and Athletic Medicine input"],
        ["Nov 25, 2026", "Final; consent form reviewed by OGC; Appendix C reviewed by ITS"],
        ["Dec 16, 2026", "In use: Kenny approves; guide posted where staff can find it"],
        ["Spring 2027", "First surveys and first annual review"],
    ], widths=[1.3, 5.4])
    d.note("Sources: NCAA SSI Performance Technologies Recommendations (March 2026); NCAA SSI "
           "webinar on performance technology and data governance (September 9, 2026); Applied "
           "Performance action plan drafts (March 2026); Software and Technology Management "
           "Framework draft and Technology Evaluation Scorecard (August 2026); Baylor Athletics "
           "technology inventory findings (September 16, 2026; final October 1, 2026), the source "
           "for product and unit counts; UT Austin SMED-8055 for structure.")
    return d


def main():
    out = HERE / "deliverables"
    out.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    jobs = [(NAME, guide)] + [
        (f"SSI_BestPractices_APPX_{key}_ER_{DATE}", fn) for key, fn in FORMS]
    for name, build in jobs:
        docx = build().save(str(out / f"{name}.docx"))
        pages = word_pdf(docx, str(out / f"{name}.pdf"))
        print(f"{name}: {pages} pages")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

1	BAYLOR ATHLETICS
2	Software and Technology Management Framework
3	1. Purpose
4	To increase the efficiency and timeliness of requests for software and technology purchase and implementation, and to establish a consistent, transparent process for how those decisions are made, reviewed, and renewed.
5	1.1  Policy statement
6	Baylor Athletics shall select, acquire, implement, use, access, disclose, retain, and dispose of software, technology, and the data they generate only for authorized athletics, sports medicine, health, safety, performance, compliance, and operational purposes, and only in accordance with Baylor University policies, applicable law, NCAA guidance, contractual obligations, and approved data-governance practices.
7	Software and technology must be governed through a written plan, routine education, defined data rights, structured technology review, and continuous improvement.
8	1.2  Reason for the framework
9	Technology used in athletics may collect biometric, health-related, performance, workload, recovery, video, sensor, survey, software, mobile-application, and other individual-level data. Responsible use of these technologies requires coordination across Athletics, Sports Medicine, Information Technology Services, Privacy, Legal, Compliance, Procurement, and Records Management.
10	This framework is intended to help Baylor Athletics support student-athlete health, safety, privacy, autonomy, data security, and performance while reducing legal, regulatory, contractual, operational, and reputational risk.
11	The framework started with athlete performance technology, which handles the most sensitive data and is subject to the clearest NCAA guidance. It is written to serve as the department's general approach to all technology. The process below applies to every technology request in the department, and the depth of review depends on the request's scope.
12	2. Scope and terminology
13	2.1  Scope
14	Technology refers to tangible items like devices, wearables, equipment, and applications. Software refers to the platforms and systems those items connect to. The two are rarely purchased independently, and this framework covers both.
15	The framework is not limited to performance, health, and wellness. Athlete performance technology sits inside that scope and triggers a review. A request that does not involve any athlete data still goes through the same review mechanism.
16	2.2  Individuals and entities affected
17	Baylor Athletics staff, coaches, sports medicine personnel, strength and conditioning staff, analysts, administrators, student support staff, and other Baylor personnel who select, use, access, interpret, or disclose technology and the data it generates.
18	Student-athletes whose data is collected, used, analyzed, inferred, stored, or disclosed through these technologies.
19	Vendors, contractors, consultants, and other third parties that collect, store, process, analyze, host, transmit, or receive Baylor Athletics data on Baylor's behalf.

To increase the efficiency and timeliness of requests for software and technology purchase and implementation, and to establish a consistent, transparent process for how those decisions are made, reviewed, and renewed.
1.1  Policy statement
Baylor Athletics shall select, acquire, implement, use, access, disclose, retain, and dispose of software, technology, and the data they generate only for authorized athletics, sports medicine, health, safety, performance, compliance, and operational purposes, and only in accordance with Baylor University policies, applicable law, NCAA guidance, contractual obligations, and approved data-governance practices.
Software and technology must be governed through a written plan, routine education, defined data rights, structured technology review, and continuous improvement.
1.2  Reason for the framework
Technology used in athletics may collect biometric, health-related, performance, workload, recovery, video, sensor, survey, software, mobile-application, and other individual-level data. Responsible use of these technologies requires coordination across Athletics, Sports Medicine, Information Technology Services, Privacy, Legal, Compliance, Procurement, and Records Management.
This framework is intended to help Baylor Athletics support student-athlete health, safety, privacy, autonomy, data security, and performance while reducing legal, regulatory, contractual, operational, and reputational risk.
The framework started with athlete performance technology, which handles the most sensitive data and is subject to the clearest NCAA guidance. It is written to serve as the department's general approach to all technology. The process below applies to every technology request in the department, and the depth of review depends on the request's scope.
2. Scope and terminology
2.1  Scope
Technology refers to tangible items like devices, wearables, equipment, and applications. Software refers to the platforms and systems those items connect to. The two are rarely purchased independently, and this framework covers both.
The framework is not limited to performance, health, and wellness. Athlete performance technology sits inside that scope and triggers a review. A request that does not involve any athlete data still goes through the same review mechanism.
2.2  Individuals and entities affected
Baylor Athletics staff, coaches, sports medicine personnel, strength and conditioning staff, analysts, administrators, student support staff, and other Baylor personnel who select, use, access, interpret, or disclose technology and the data it generates.
Student-athletes whose data is collected, used, analyzed, inferred, stored, or disclosed through these technologies.
Vendors, contractors, consultants, and other third parties that collect, store, process, analyze, host, transmit, or receive Baylor Athletics data on Baylor's behalf.
Baylor units supporting Athletics, including ITS, Information Security, Office of General Counsel, University Compliance and Risk Services, Privacy, Internal Audit, Procurement, and records-management functions.
2.3  Exclusions
This framework does not replace or supersede Baylor policies that already govern specific categories of data, systems, conduct, records, or legal obligations. Where a more specific Baylor policy applies, that policy continues to govern. This document should be read as an Athletics-specific overlay that routes technology decisions into existing Baylor governance channels rather than around them.
2.4  Definitions

That guidance sets the expectations each institution is to meet and leaves the method of implementation to the institution, according to its own structure and resources. This framework is Baylor Athletics' implementation. Appendix A maps each NCAA recommendation to the section of this framework that carries it.

Coordinated renewal and term review, giving the department advance visibility of contract end dates and the lead time to evaluate options well before a renewal decision is due.
Increased staff fluency so that sport administrators and unit staff can address technology questions with confidence.

6. Levels of review
The level of review depends on three things: what data the technology touches, how many units it serves, and what the department is committing to in cost and contract term.

7. Exceptions
7.1  Urgent and “emergency” requests

This provides documentation for what qualifies as urgent, so the distinction does not have to be determined on a case-by-case basis at intake. 1.5  The request is evaluated against the Technology Evaluation Scorecard.

    python build_outline_filled.py        (run from scripts/)

NAME = f"SSI_BestPractices_OUTLINE_FILLED_KENNY_ER_{DATE}"
SOP = "SOP (Software and Technology Management Framework, Aug 14 draft)"

DECISIONS = [
    ["1. Guide or formal policy?", "A best-practices guide with forms. A one-page policy statement only if you want one."],
    ["2. How does it fit the SOP?", "The SOP runs the request and review process. This guide adds what the SOP lists as \"planned for Version 1\"."],
    ["3. Scope?", "Four areas (adoption, consent, vendor contracts, staff transition) plus a short education section."],
]

# (section, already in the SOP, this guide adds). One row per outline section.
COVERAGE = [
    ["0. Purpose and scope", "Policy statement, scope, definitions (§1–2)", "Principles; notice and consent terms"],
    ["1. Governance", "Roles; weekly ITS meeting (§5, §8)", "Technology Review; Data Steward; annual review"],
    ["2. Technology adoption", "Full request process; Levels 1–3 (§6, §8)", "Start from the question; one scoring sheet; quality checks"],
    ["3. Consent and education", "Training required; athlete notice (§2.4, §5)", "Consent form; education program"],
    ["4. Data management", "Data classes; ITS and OGC review roles (§2.4, §5)", "Ownership; storage; access; uses; transfer athletes"],
    ["5. Vendor contracts", "Procurement checks contract terms (§5)", "14-term checklist; exit and deletion; contract review"],
    ["6. Staff transition", "Nothing", "All of it (original work)"],
    ["7. Continuous improvement", "Usage review at 6 months or season end (§8 Phase 3)", "Athlete and staff surveys; annual review"],
]

# Fills each outline part, keyed by the part name in build_outline.SECTIONS.
FILL = {
    # 0
    "Purpose statement": "Baylor's written plan under the NCAA SSI recommendations (March 2026): how we choose technology, handle athlete data, educate people and improve. The SOP's policy statement (§1.1) stays the policy.",
    "Definitions (NCAA SSI terms)": "Use the SOP's definitions (§2.4). Add only: performance, physiologic and cognitive data; notice versus consent; Data Steward; custodian.",
    "Who it applies to": "Same people as the SOP (§2.2): staff, coaches, interns, contractors, student-athletes and vendors. Baylor University policy still governs where it applies (§2.3).",
    "Guiding principles": "Start from the question. Data guided, not data driven. Collect only what we use. Athletic Medicine decides return to play. Athletes know, and athletes choose.",
    # 1
    "Technology Review: when and where it meets": "A standing item at an existing staff meeting, not a new committee. Multidisciplinary; a SAAC athlete is invited. Decides Level 3 requests. Fills the SOP's planned Working Group. [Kenny: which meeting]",
    "Data Steward role": "Director of Applied Performance, with a named backup. Keeps the inventory, the consent register and the release log, and runs offboarding. Adds data duties to the SOP's point-of-contact role (§5).",
    "Review and version control": "Reviewed each spring, and when NCAA, Big 12 or Baylor policy changes. Numbered versions; master copy in a shared Athletics location.",
    "Medical authority (Athletic Medicine)": "Athletic Medicine holds full authority over medical and return-to-play decisions. Data informs; it does not decide. Builds on the SOP's Health & Wellness role (§5).",
    # 2
    "Request and review process (Software and Technology Management Framework)": "Use the SOP as written: Idea Form and ATH Form, Business Office, ITS, decision (§8 Phase 1); review depth by Level 1–3 (§6). The guide does not repeat it.",
    "Start from the question; one scoring sheet": "Each request names its question, who acts on it and how often. One scoring sheet (Appendix E) merges the March checklist and the SOP scorecard (§8, 1.5).",
    "Quality checks before commitment": "Independent evidence; the vendor explains derived scores; a 30–60 day trial when evidence is weak; ask two peer programs; check the inventory for a tool we already own.",
    # 3
    "Notice and consent": "Notice (told): video, team GPS and venue tracking, training-program testing. Consent (asked; can say no): wearables outside sessions, body composition, cognitive testing, research. Saying no costs nothing. [OGC: final split]",
    "Consent form and when it is signed": "Appendix A. Signed each year and when a new technology starts in the sport. Parent signs for athletes under 18. OGC reviews before first use.",
    "Vendor norm-building": "A vendor pools Baylor data only with written agreement. Athletes are told which vendors have one.",
    "Where consent records live": "With the athlete's Athletic Medicine record. The Data Steward keeps a register staff check before collecting. [Athletic Medicine: system]",
    "Education by group": "Applied Performance builds and runs it, once a year per group (staff, athletes, coaches; new staff within 30 days), on SSI's four topics. Start from the education materials Applied Performance already has on Box.",

class KennyDoc:
    """Same calls as BaylorDoc: meta, callout, section, subhead, para, note,
    small, bullets, numbered, quote, table, page_break, spacer, save."""

    def __init__(self, title, deck=None, status=None, **_ignored):
        self.doc = Document(str(TEMPLATE))
        self.status = status
        self._title = title
        self._list_count = 0
        self._footer_line(title, status)
        p = self.doc.add_paragraph(); tight(p)

Kenny Boyd (reviewer on the Baylor Athletics Software and Technology Management
Framework) consistently pushes back on three things in draft policy language:

1. **No language that implies the department was previously incompetent.** He cut
   "so the department stops discovering it is in the final year of an agreement
   with no time to act" for exactly this reason. Rewrite as forward-looking
   capability ("advance visibility of contract end dates and the lead time to
   evaluate options"), not as a problem being fixed.
2. **No judgmental or ranking-flavored labels.** He rejected the Light / Standard /
   Elevated review tiers. Neutral, descriptive, escalating names work better —
   Level 1 Standard / Level 2 Enhanced / Level 3 Comprehensive Review. He floated
   Basic / Intermediate / Advanced, which reads as sophistication of the
   *technology* rather than depth of *review*.
3. **Name the seniority of the reviewer, not just the office.** For ITS he wanted
   it clear that a supervisory-level person with authority to commit resources is
   involved, not a line technician. Frame this as decision authority the request
   requires, never as competence of the staff.

He also wants Baylor branding carried through headers/footers and draft status
marked on every page.

**Why:** These are tone constraints, not content ones — the same facts land or
fail on phrasing. Getting them wrong costs a full review cycle.

**How to apply:** Before sending any Athletics policy or framework draft for his
review, scan for blame-implying rationale, ranking adjectives on process tiers,
and unqualified office names where seniority matters.

content.text:
Base directory for this skill: /Users/kristinarash/.claude/skills/memory-write

# Memory Write

## Outcome
- Fact added to, updated in, or removed from the correct memory tier
- Tier-B caps enforced (2,500 chars for MEMORY.md, 1,375 for USER.md)
- Confirmation: "Saved — will be active from next session."

## Pick the tier first

Ask: "Will this fact still be true and useful in 3 months, across multiple projects?"

**Tier A — `~/.claude/projects/<slug>/memory/`** (one file per fact, indexed by MEMORY.md)
- Durable user facts → `user_*.md` (metadata.type: user)
- Stable project conventions / gotchas → `project_*.md` (metadata.type: project)
- Behavioral feedback rules → `feedback_*.md` (metadata.type: feedback)
- External-system pointers → `reference_*.md` (metadata.type: reference)

**Tier B — `~/.claude/global-memory/`** (single capped file)
- Active threads (in-progress work) → `MEMORY.md` `## Active Threads`
- Current env notes (URLs, tool versions, project structure in play) → `MEMORY.md` `## Environment Notes`
- Pending decisions → `MEMORY.md` `## Pending Decisions`
- Durable user profile updates → `USER.md`

## Steps

1. **Decide tier** using the rule above.
2. **Read** the target file in full.
3. **Dedup check** — substring scan; if the fact already exists, skip or update in place.
4. **Cap check** for Tier B — `wc -c < ~/.claude/global-memory/MEMORY.md` (or USER.md). If over cap, consolidate (merge similar entries, prune stale) before adding.
5. **Write** the change.
   - Tier A: create a new file with proper frontmatter (name, description, metadata.type) and add a one-line pointer to that slug's `MEMORY.md` index. `name:` follows the rule below. Do it in one call, from the project folder (the slug comes from the current folder; `--dir` overrides):
     `python3 ~/.claude/scripts/remember.py --type <t> --name <bare-slug> --desc "<one line>" --hook "<when to open>" [--why "..." --how "..."] "<fact>"`
     It checks the name rule, refuses an existing or look-alike name (exit 2: read that file, then `--update` it or `--force`), writes the file and the index line, runs steps 1 and 4 of the Verification Gate, and refreshes recall.py's index. `PASS` covers those checks; step 3 (contradictions) is still yours.
   - Tier B: append under the correct `##` section.
6. **Confirm** in one line: `Saved — will be active from next session.`

## The `name:` field — bare kebab slug

**`name:` = the filename stem minus its leading type token, kebab-cased.** The type
already lives in `metadata.type` and the filename already carries the prefix; repeating
it in `name:` is the third copy.

| File | `name:` |
|---|---|
| `project_automation-cadence.md` | `automation-cadence` |
| `user_sports-teams.md` | `sports-teams` |
| `reference_baylor-house-style.md` | `baylor-house-style` |
| `feedback_project_idea_capture.md` | `project-idea-capture` |

Note the last row: strip only the **leading** token. `feedback_project_idea_capture.md`
is a feedback memory *about* project-idea capture — its name keeps the word `project`.

`[[links]]` target this bare name, never the filename and never a prefixed variant.

This rule exists because it was previously unwritten: an audit on 2026-09-02 found the
corpus split 59 bare / 58 prefixed, which broke 37 links. Both forms look right in
isolation, so without a stated rule the split regrows on every write.

## Actions

- **add** — append (default)
- **replace** — substring match + swap. Preferred over add when updating an existing fact.
- **remove** — confirm with the user before deleting.

## Retrieval — the tiered ladder

When the user asks about past context, decisions, or "did we already…?", climb in order and stop as soon as the question is answered. Do not run a search when the answer is already in the injected snapshot.

1. **Tier 0** — scan what is already in context (USER.md, MEMORY.md, today's compiled log). Zero cost.
2. **L1** — `python3 ~/.claude/scripts/recall.py "question"`. Plain code, ~1 s: BM25 keyword rank over the memsearch paths plus the whole vault, a Tier A memory first, then it opens the best file and prints the matching paragraphs with line numbers. On a weak or no match it also runs memsearch (~10 s) and prints its hits. Answer from that. If the printed paragraphs miss the answer, open the #2 or #3 candidate it lists.
3. **L2** — when L1's output (memsearch hits included) still misses: `python3 ~/.claude/scripts/recall.py "<reworded query>" --deep`. Its memsearch section is hybrid vector + keyword, ~10 s, memory files first: the Mac Tier A slugs listed in `memory-index-paths.json` (recall.py reads every slug, Windows ones included), daily logs, transcripts, handoffs, audits.
4. **L3** — `memsearch expand <chunk_hash>`. Full markdown section around a hit.
5. **L4** — `memsearch transcript <session_id>`. Raw dialogue. Last resort.
6. **Fallback** — say "I don't have a record of that."

**A recall that turned out wrong or stale becomes a test question — without being asked.** When Eric corrects a recalled fact, or you find that the answer you gave from recall was outdated (a newer file says otherwise), add the question to the bench yourself in the same session: one row in `~/.claude/scripts/recall-bench/questions.tsv` (set `miss`, the question as asked, the file holding the right answer, the right answer in one line), then run `CSET=miss bash ~/.claude/scripts/recall-bench/run.sh C` (~Feedback.06 a question) and note the result in that folder's `results.md`. Say so in one line. Eric will not remember to ask; the daily backup's recall check (`recall-bench/check.py`) then guards that question from then on.

## Daily compiled logs — read-only

`~/.claude/claude-memory-compiler/daily/{YYYY-MM-DD}.md` is produced by `claude-memory-compiler` through its own SessionEnd/PreCompact hooks, and injected by its own SessionStart hook.

- **Never hand-edit these files.** The compiler owns them.
- **Never read them eagerly.** Treat the injected snapshot as the source of truth.

## What is loaded at session start

`~/.claude/global-memory/USER.md` and `MEMORY.md` are read once at session start and are a **frozen snapshot**. Mid-session writes persist to disk but only take effect next session — this is deliberate, to preserve the prefix cache. Never load more than the startup set proactively.

## Rules

- Never exceed Tier B caps. Consolidate first.
- Always dedup before adding.
- For Tier A, the slug is the absolute cwd with every character other than a letter or digit replaced by `-` (Mac `~/DEV` → `-Users-kristinarash-DEV`, `~/.claude/skills` → `-Users-kristinarash--claude-skills`; `_` folds too: `~/DEV/CLI_Dev` → `-Users-kristinarash-DEV-CLI-Dev`, verified 2026-10-24; Windows `~/Desktop/DEV` → `C--Users-eric-rash-Desktop-DEV`; `00_Primary_Storage_Drive` → `00-Primary-Storage-Drive`). The harness injects the correct slug each session — use that, don't reconstruct it.
- **Write only to the current machine's slug.** Mac slugs are `-Users-kristinarash-*`; Windows desktop-app sessions (the laptop has had no automation since 2026-10-14) write `C--Users-eric-rash-*`. A fact written to the other machine's slug is never auto-injected here (recall.py still finds it; memsearch indexes only the Mac slugs). Durable project facts belong in the repo's `docs/` so both machines see them.
- Never announce the write mid-session beyond the one-line confirmation. The injected snapshot is frozen — the new fact appears next session, not this one.

## Verification Gate

After every write:

1. Read the exact destination back and require the intended fact to appear once in the intended tier.
2. Re-run the Tier B character cap check after the write.
3. Check the surrounding section for an unresolved contradiction or stale duplicate. Resolve it or report `FAIL`.
4. For Tier A, verify the new file has valid frontmatter and the memory index pointer resolves to it.
5. Distinguish persisted state from activation: the write can pass now, but next-session injection remains unverified until a later session observes it.

Report `PASS` only when persistence, uniqueness, tier placement, caps, and pointers are verified. Report `FAIL` with the target path and failed check otherwise. Do not emit “Saved” before read-back succeeds.

content.text:
# Update Config Skill

Modify Claude Code configuration by updating settings.json files.

## When Hooks Are Required (Not Memory)

If the user wants something to happen automatically in response to an EVENT, they need a **hook** configured in settings.json. Memory/preferences cannot trigger automated actions.

**These require hooks:**
- "Before compacting, ask me what to preserve" → PreCompact hook
- "After writing files, run prettier" → PostToolUse hook with Write|Edit matcher
- "When I run bash commands, log them" → PreToolUse hook with Bash matcher
- "Always run tests after code changes" → PostToolUse hook

**Hook events:** PreToolUse, PostToolUse, PreCompact, PostCompact, Stop, Notification, SessionStart

## CRITICAL: Read Before Write

**Always read the existing settings file before making changes.** Merge new settings with existing ones - never replace the entire file.

## CRITICAL: Use AskUserQuestion for Ambiguity

When the user's request is ambiguous, use AskUserQuestion to clarify:
- Which settings file to modify (user/project/local)
- Whether to add to existing arrays or replace them
- Specific values when multiple options exist

## Decision: /config command vs Direct Edit

**Suggest the `/config` slash command** for these simple settings:
- `theme`, `editorMode`, `verbose`, `model`
- `language`, `alwaysThinkingEnabled`
- `permissions.defaultMode`

**Edit settings.json directly** for:
- Hooks (PreToolUse, PostToolUse, etc.)
- Complex permission rules (allow/deny arrays)
- Environment variables
- MCP server configuration
- Plugin configuration

## Workflow

1. **Clarify intent** - Ask if the request is ambiguous
2. **Read existing file** - Use Read tool on the target settings file
3. **Merge carefully** - Preserve existing settings, especially arrays
4. **Edit file** - Use Edit tool (if file doesn't exist, ask user to create it first)
5. **Confirm** - Tell user what was changed

## Merging Arrays (Important!)

When adding to permission arrays or hook arrays, **merge with existing**, don't replace:

**WRONG** (replaces existing permissions):
```json
{ "permissions": { "allow": ["Bash(npm *)"] } }
```

**RIGHT** (preserves existing + adds new):
```json
{
  "permissions": {
    "allow": [
      "Bash(git *)",      // existing
      "Edit(.claude)",    // existing
      "Bash(npm *)"       // new
    ]
  }
}
```

## Settings File Locations

Choose the appropriate file based on scope:

| File | Scope | Git | Use For |
|------|-------|-----|---------|
| `~/.claude/settings.json` | Global | N/A | Personal preferences for all projects |
| `.claude/settings.json` | Project | Commit | Team-wide hooks, permissions, plugins |
| `.claude/settings.local.json` | Project | Gitignore | Personal overrides for this project |

Settings load in order: user → project → local (later overrides earlier).

## Settings Schema Reference

### Permissions
```json
{
  "permissions": {
    "allow": ["Bash(npm *)", "Edit(.claude)", "Read"],
    "deny": ["Bash(rm -rf *)"],
    "ask": ["Edit(//etc/*)"],
    "defaultMode": "default" | "plan" | "acceptEdits" | "dontAsk",
    "additionalDirectories": ["/extra/dir"]
  }
}
```

**Permission Rule Syntax:**
- Exact match: `"Bash(npm run test)"`
- Prefix wildcard: `"Bash(git *)"` - matches `git`, `git status`, `git commit`, etc.
- Tool only: `"Read"` - allows all Read operations
- File paths: `"Edit(src/**)"` - path rules in `permissions` use `Edit(path)` for every file-writing tool (Write, Edit, NotebookEdit) and `Read(path)` for reads. `Write(path)`, `NotebookEdit(path)` and `Glob(path)` rules are not matched by file permission checks. Bare tool names (`"Write"`), deny/ask `Tool(param:value)` rules and hook `if` conditions still use each tool's own name

### Environment Variables
```json
{
  "env": {
    "DEBUG": "true",
    "MY_API_KEY": "value"
  }
}
```

### Model & Agent
```json
{
  "model": "sonnet",  // or "fable", "opus", "haiku", full model ID
  "agent": "agent-name",
  "alwaysThinkingEnabled": true
}
```

### Attribution (Commits & PRs)
```json
{
  "attribution": {
    "commit": "Custom commit trailer text",
    "pr": "Custom PR description text"
  }
}
```
Set `commit` or `pr` to empty string `""` to hide that attribution. To hide all of it, set both to `""` and also set `"sessionUrl": false`. Write this object form, not `"attribution": false`: older Claude Code versions reject true or false here and then skip the whole settings file.

### MCP Server Management
```json
{
  "enableAllProjectMcpServers": true,
  "enabledMcpjsonServers": ["server1", "server2"],
  "disabledMcpjsonServers": ["blocked-server"]
}
```

### Plugins
```json
{
  "enabledPlugins": {
    "formatter@anthropic-tools": true
  }
}
```
Plugin syntax: `plugin-name@source` where source is `claude-code-marketplace`, `claude-plugins-official`, or `builtin`.

### Other Settings
- `language`: Preferred response language (e.g., "japanese")
- `cleanupPeriodDays`: Days to keep transcripts before automatic cleanup (default: 30; minimum 1)
- `respectGitignore`: Whether to respect .gitignore (default: true)
- `spinnerTipsEnabled`: Show tips in spinner
- `timeFormat`: Clock format for times shown in the UI: "auto" (default), "12-hour", "24-hour", "24-hour-utc", or a strftime pattern such as "%H:%M"
- `timeZone`: IANA time zone for times shown in the UI, e.g. "UTC" (default: system time zone)
- `spinnerVerbs`: Customize spinner verbs (`{ "mode": "append" | "replace", "verbs": [...] }`)
- `spinnerTipsOverride`: Override spinner tips (`{ "excludeDefault": true, "tips": ["Custom tip"] }`)
- `syntaxHighlightingDisabled`: Disable diff highlighting


## Hooks Configuration

Hooks run commands at specific points in Claude Code's lifecycle.

### Hook Structure
```json
{
  "hooks": {
    "EVENT_NAME": [
      {
        "matcher": "ToolName|OtherTool",
        "hooks": [
          {
            "type": "command",
            "command": "your-command-here",
            "timeout": 60,
            "statusMessage": "Running..."
          }
        ]
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

### Hook Events

| Event | Matcher | Purpose |
|-------|---------|---------|
| PermissionRequest | Tool name | Run before permission prompt |
| PreToolUse | Tool name | Run before tool, can block |
| PostToolUse | Tool name | Run after successful tool |
| PostToolUseFailure | Tool name | Run after tool fails |
| Notification | Notification type | Run on notifications |
| Stop | - | Run when Claude stops (including clear, resume, compact) |
| PreCompact | "manual"/"auto" | Before compaction |
| PostCompact | "manual"/"auto" | After compaction (receives summary) |
| UserPromptSubmit | - | When user submits |
| SessionStart | - | When session starts |

**Common tool matchers:** `Bash`, `Write`, `Edit`, `Read`, `Glob`, `Grep`

### Hook Types

**1. Command Hook** - Runs a shell command:
```json
{ "type": "command", "command": "prettier --write $FILE", "timeout": 30 }
```

**2. Prompt Hook** - Evaluates a condition with LLM:
```json
{ "type": "prompt", "prompt": "Is this safe? $ARGUMENTS" }
```
Only available for tool events: PreToolUse, PostToolUse, PermissionRequest.

**3. Agent Hook** - Runs an agent with tools:
```json
{ "type": "agent", "prompt": "Verify tests pass: $ARGUMENTS" }
```
Only available for tool events: PreToolUse, PostToolUse, PermissionRequest.

### Hook Input (stdin JSON)
```json
{
  "session_id": "abc123",
  "tool_name": "Write",
  "tool_input": { "file_path": "/path/to/file.txt", "content": "..." },
  "tool_response": { "success": true }  // PostToolUse only
}
```

### Hook JSON Output

Hooks can return JSON to control behavior:

```json
{
  "systemMessage": "Warning shown to user in UI",
  "continue": false,
  "stopReason": "Message shown when blocking",
  "suppressOutput": false,
  "decision": "block",
  "reason": "Explanation for decision",
  "hookSpecificOutput": {
    "hookEventName": "PostToolUse",
    "additionalContext": "Context injected back to model"
  }
}
```

**Fields:**
- `systemMessage` - Display a message to the user (all hooks)
- `continue` - Set to `false` to block/stop (default: true)
- `stopReason` - Message shown when `continue` is false
- `suppressOutput` - Hide stdout from transcript (default: false)
- `decision` - "block" for PostToolUse/Stop/UserPromptSubmit hooks (deprecated for PreToolUse, use hookSpecificOutput.permissionDecision instead)
- `reason` - Explanation for decision
- `hookSpecificOutput` - Event-specific output (must include `hookEventName`):
  - `additionalContext` - Text injected into model context
  - `permissionDecision` - "allow", "deny", or "ask" (PreToolUse only)
  - `permissionDecisionReason` - Reason for the permission decision (PreToolUse only)
  - `updatedInput` - Modified tool input (PreToolUse only)

### Common Patterns

**Auto-format after writes:**
```json
{
  "hooks": {
    "PostToolUse": [{
      "matcher": "Write|Edit",
      "hooks": [{
        "type": "command",
        "command": "jq -r '.tool_response.filePath // .tool_input.file_path' | { read -r f; prettier --write \"$f\"; } 2>/dev/null || true"
      }]
    }]
  }
}
```

**Log all bash commands:**
```json
{
  "hooks": {
    "PreToolUse": [{
      "matcher": "Bash",
      "hooks": [{
        "type": "command",
        "command": "jq -r '.tool_input.command' >> ~/.claude/bash-log.txt"
      }]
    }]
  }
}
```

**Stop hook that displays message to user:**

Command must output JSON with `systemMessage` field:
```bash
# Example command that outputs: {"systemMessage": "Session complete!"}
echo '{"systemMessage": "Session complete!"}'
```

**Run tests after code changes:**
```json
{
  "hooks": {
    "PostToolUse": [{
      "matcher": "Write|Edit",
      "hooks": [{
        "type": "command",
        "command": "jq -r '.tool_input.file_path // .tool_response.filePath' | grep -E '\\.(ts|js)$' && npm test || true"
      }]
    }]
  }
}
```


## Constructing a Hook (with verification)

Given an event, matcher, target file, and desired behavior, follow this flow. Each step catches a different failure class — a hook that silently does nothing is worse than no hook.

1. **Dedup check.** Read the target file. If a hook already exists on the same event+matcher, show the existing command and ask: keep it, replace it, or add alongside.

2. **Construct the command for THIS project — don't assume.** The hook receives JSON on stdin. Build a command that:
   - Extracts any needed payload safely — use `jq -r` into a quoted variable or `{ read -r f; ... "$f"; }`, NOT unquoted `| xargs` (splits on spaces)
   - Invokes the underlying tool the way this project runs it (npx/bunx/yarn/pnpm? Makefile target? globally-installed?)
   - Skips inputs the tool doesn't handle (formatters often have `--ignore-unknown`; if not, guard by extension)
   - Stays RAW for now — no `|| true`, no stderr suppression. You'll wrap it after the pipe-test passes.

3. **Pipe-test the raw command.** Synthesize the stdin payload the hook will receive and pipe it directly:
   - `Pre|PostToolUse` on `Write|Edit`: `echo '{"tool_name":"Edit","tool_input":{"file_path":"<a real file from this repo>"}}' | <cmd>`
   - `Pre|PostToolUse` on `Bash`: `echo '{"tool_name":"Bash","tool_input":{"command":"ls"}}' | <cmd>`
   - `Stop`/`UserPromptSubmit`/`SessionStart`: most commands don't read stdin, so `echo '{}' | <cmd>` suffices

   Check exit code AND side effect (file actually formatted, test actually ran). If it fails you get a real error — fix (wrong package manager? tool not installed? jq path wrong?) and retest. Once it works, wrap with `2>/dev/null || true` (unless the user wants a blocking check).

4. **Write the JSON.** Merge into the target file (schema shape in the "Hook Structure" section above). If this creates `.claude/settings.local.json` for the first time, add it to .gitignore — the Write tool doesn't auto-gitignore it.

5. **Validate syntax + schema in one shot:**

   `jq -e '.hooks.<event>[] | select(.matcher == "<matcher>") | .hooks[] | select(.type == "command") | .command' <target-file>`

   Exit 0 + prints your command = correct. Exit 4 = matcher doesn't match. Exit 5 = malformed JSON or wrong nesting. A broken settings.json silently disables ALL settings from that file — fix any pre-existing malformation too.

6. **Prove the hook fires** — only for `Pre|PostToolUse` on a matcher you can trigger in-turn (`Write|Edit` via Edit, `Bash` via Bash). `Stop`/`UserPromptSubmit`/`SessionStart` fire outside this turn — skip to step 7.

   For a **formatter** on `PostToolUse`/`Write|Edit`: introduce a detectable violation via Edit (two consecutive blank lines, bad indentation, missing semicolon — something this formatter corrects; NOT trailing whitespace, Edit strips that before writing), re-read, confirm the hook **fixed** it. For **anything else**: temporarily prefix the command in settings.json with `echo "$(date) hook fired" >> /tmp/claude-hook-check.txt; `, trigger the matching tool (Edit for `Write|Edit`, a harmless `true` for `Bash`), read the sentinel file.

   **Always clean up** — revert the violation, strip the sentinel prefix — whether the proof passed or failed.

   **If proof fails but pipe-test passed and `jq -e` passed**: the settings watcher isn't watching `.claude/` — it only watches directories that had a settings file when this session started. The hook is written correctly. Tell the user to open `/hooks` once (reloads config) or restart — you can't do this yourself; `/hooks` is a user UI menu and opening it ends this turn.

7. **Handoff.** Tell the user the hook is live (or needs `/hooks`/restart per the watcher caveat). Point them at `/hooks` to review, edit, or disable it later. The UI only shows "Ran N hooks" if a hook errors or is slow — silent success is invisible by design.


## Example Workflows

### Adding a Hook

User: "Format my code after Claude writes it"

1. **Clarify**: Which formatter? (prettier, gofmt, etc.)
2. **Read**: `.claude/settings.json` (or create if missing)
3. **Merge**: Add to existing hooks, don't replace
4. **Result**:
```json
{
  "hooks": {
    "PostToolUse": [{
      "matcher": "Write|Edit",
      "hooks": [{
        "type": "command",
        "command": "jq -r '.tool_response.filePath // .tool_input.file_path' | { read -r f; prettier --write \"$f\"; } 2>/dev/null || true"
      }]
    }]
  }
}
```

### Adding Permissions

User: "Allow npm commands without prompting"

1. **Read**: Existing permissions
2. **Merge**: Add `Bash(npm *)` to allow array
3. **Result**: Combined with existing allows

### Environment Variables

User: "Set DEBUG=true"

1. **Decide**: User settings (global) or project settings?
2. **Read**: Target file
3. **Merge**: Add to env object
```json
{ "env": { "DEBUG": "true" } }
```

## Common Mistakes to Avoid

1. **Replacing instead of merging** - Always preserve existing settings
2. **Wrong file** - Ask user if scope is unclear
3. **Invalid JSON** - Validate syntax after changes
4. **Forgetting to read first** - Always read before write

## Troubleshooting Hooks

If a hook isn't running:
1. **Check the settings file** - Read ~/.claude/settings.json or .claude/settings.json
2. **Verify JSON syntax** - Invalid JSON silently fails
3. **Check the matcher** - Does it match the tool name? (e.g., "Bash", "Write", "Edit")
4. **Check hook type** - Is it "command", "prompt", or "agent"?
5. **Test the command** - Run the hook command manually to see if it works
6. **Use --debug** - Run `claude --debug` to see hook execution logs


## Full Settings JSON Schema

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "$schema": {
      "description": "JSON Schema reference for Claude Code settings",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "apiKeyHelper": {
      "description": "Path to a script that outputs authentication values",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "proxyAuthHelper": {
      "description": "Shell command that outputs a Proxy-Authorization header value (EAP)",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "awsCredentialExport": {
      "description": "Path to a script that exports AWS credentials",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "awsAuthRefresh": {
      "description": "Path to a script that refreshes AWS authentication",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "gcpAuthRefresh": {
      "description": "Command to refresh GCP authentication (e.g., gcloud auth application-default login)",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "processWrapper": {
      "description": "Corporate launcher argv prefix for the background-agent supervisor, the sessions and workers it hosts, and the other covered background processes listed in the Claude Code corporate-launcher documentation. Equivalent to the CLAUDE_CODE_PROCESS_WRAPPER environment variable, which takes precedence when set. Honored from managed settings, a --settings/SDK-supplied settings file, and user settings, in that precedence order; project and local settings are ignored.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "policyHelper": {
      "description": "Executable that computes managed settings at startup. Honored only from admin-controlled policy sources.",
      "type": "object",
      "properties": {

A session on a provider that is not listed is refused at startup, at login, and when it next contacts the API, with a message naming what selected the provider and the entry that would allow it. Under a list, where first-party traffic goes (ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL, a gateway sign-in) is honored only when the same managed source pins it in \"env\" (or forceLoginGatewayUrl), and a claude ssh tunnel into the machine is refused. A cloud provider's credential and tenancy variables, and the network path and TLS trust (HTTPS_PROXY, NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS, CLAUDE_CODE_CERT_STORE), are not judged by this list; set those for the fleet in the managed \"env\" block, whose values replace the user's. To route Bedrock through a gateway for a fleet, pin ANTHROPIC_BEDROCK_BASE_URL there (it is what the clients use, ahead of an endpoint_url in ~/.aws/config, which this list does not judge); the AWS SDK's AWS_ENDPOINT_URL* pins only sanction where the SDK's own clients go and never stand in for the \"bedrock\" entry. Unset allows every provider; an empty array allows none. Only a list in managed-settings.json or MDM is enforcement on the machine: it cannot be widened or hidden by server-managed settings and reaches every session. A list set only in the admin console reaches only sessions that fetch your server-managed settings — not a session on a cloud provider, another organization or a non-Anthropic ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL, one authenticating only with apiKeyHelper or ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN, a Pro/Max login, --bare without an API key, or a first launch before the fetch lands — all conditions the user controls. Intended for deployments whose goal is egress control rather than filesystem containment.           "description": "Linux only: Run without the fresh /proc mount, for hosts such as unprivileged Docker containers that cannot create one. **Reduces security** — the host /proc stays readable by sandboxed commands.         "allowNestedUserNamespaces": {
          "description": "Linux/WSL only: Let sandboxed commands create user namespaces of their own, which the sandbox refuses by default. Default: false. Only honored from user, managed/policy, or CLI (--settings) settings — true from project settings (.claude/settings.json and .claude/settings.local.json) is ignored (false there still applies).",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "enableWeakerNetworkIsolation": {
          "description": "macOS only: Allow access to com.apple.trustd.agent in the sandbox. Needed for Go-based CLI tools (gh, gcloud, terraform, etc.) to verify TLS certificates when using httpProxyPort with a MITM proxy and custom CA. **Reduces security** — opens a potential data exfiltration vector through the trustd service. Default: false. When managed settings or a --settings file set allowUnsandboxedCommands: false, or managed settings set network.allowManagedDomainsOnly: true, true from project settings (.claude/settings.json and .claude/settings.local.json) is ignored (false there still applies).",

Only honored from user, managed/policy, or CLI (--settings) settings — project settings (.claude/settings.json and .claude/settings.local.json) are ignored. Default: false",

Your permission settings stop me from editing `~/.claude/settings.json`. That guard is on purpose, so I will not go around it. You can add the rules yourself in one step.

**Do this:** paste the line below into the prompt. The `!` runs it in this session. It saves a backup first, adds both rules, and keeps every rule you already have.

```

- **Allow rule** `Bash(gws drive files create:*)`: a plain upload runs with no prompt.

   capability ("advance visibility of contract end dates and the lead time to
   evaluate options"), not as a problem being fixed.
2. **No judgmental or ranking-flavored labels.** He rejected the Light / Standard /
   Elevated review tiers. Neutral, descriptive, escalating names work better —
   Level 1 Standard / Level 2 Enhanced / Level 3 Comprehensive Review. He floated
   Basic / Intermediate / Advanced, which reads as sophistication of the
   *technology* rather than depth of *review*.
3. **Name the seniority of the reviewer, not just the office.** For ITS he wanted
   it clear that a supervisory-level person with authority to commit resources is
   involved, not a line technician. Frame this as decision authority the request
   requires, never as competence of the staff.

He also wants Baylor branding carried through headers/footers and draft status
marked on every page.

Format (his own words, Tech Sync 2026-10-28): no long wordy documents; "economy of
words"; a clean cover with the details behind it; charts and trend lines over
text ("not a pre-K version" either). Say plainly when something already exists
("we already have this") so work is not duplicated. To him "the SOP" means the
Software and Technology Management Framework.

**Why:** These are tone constraints, not content ones — the same facts land or
fail on phrasing. Getting them wrong costs a full review cycle.

**How to apply:** Before sending any Athletics policy or framework draft for his
review, scan for blame-implying rationale, ranking adjectives on process tiers,
and unqualified office names where seniority matters.
